Title: The Gullet of Gorm
Synopsis: Hired by the town of Dunmarrow to see to a problem with the plumbing, four inspectors walk twenty floors down the throat of a sleeping god. Each tier is a station of a pilgrimage nobody told them they were on: the Skin, the Gut, the Heart, the Dream. At the bottom waits the verger who has kept Gorm asleep for three hundred years on a diet of four adventurers a generation.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a dry, precise church verger of great age; liturgical cadence, offended by noise and blood, never raised

Cast.Name: Maud Sorrel
Cast.Role: A sleepwalking guide who is always one floor further down than she should be, and always dry
Cast.Secret: She drowned in the Gullet thirty-eight years ago; what walks and speaks is Gorm's dream wearing her. It comes out on floor 18 when she sits down and speaks as Him.

Persona.VoiceStyle: an old woman talking in her sleep: unhurried, kind, faintly amused at the size of everything

Cast.Name: Alderman Hesketh Crane
Cast.Role: The employer, who follows the party down to check the invoice and keeps finding paperwork he wrote
Cast.Secret: He carved the party's names on the memorial stone before they left, and has done it four times. It comes out on floor 17, with the gas rising, just before he sells them.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a plump market-town alderman; bluster over panic, speaks in clauses, invoices and apologies

Cast.Name: Deacon Tobit Hale
Cast.Role: The Verger's junior, sent up to greet the congregation, desperate for the work to be holy
Cast.Secret: Quill is grooming him as the next gag in Gorm's mouth and means to stop being human. It lands on floor 16, by which time he has either defected or been used.

Persona.VoiceStyle: an eager young deacon, polite to a fault, delighted to have visitors at last

Cast.Name: Grisel Thorn
Cast.Role: Sole survivor of the last four, nineteen years in the Gut, keeps a camp under a spider's shell
Cast.Secret: She bought her life by walking her own party to the jailers, and has gone on doing it. It comes out on floor 9 when Crane reads the old contract aloud.

Persona.VoiceStyle: nineteen years alone underground: flat, wry, addresses people like spiders she already knows

Cast.Name: Old Ulf
Cast.Role: Keeper of the Forge, who will tell you cheerfully that he casts tools
Cast.Secret: He knows exactly what the moulds cast, and is proud of every baby in Dunmarrow. It comes out on floor 13 when he shows the faces off like plate.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a jovial old founder, soot in his beard, proud of his work and deaf to what it means

Mystery.Question: Why does Dunmarrow send four inspectors down the Gullet every nineteen years?
Mystery.Truth: The council has a standing contract with the Verger: four souls a generation keep Gorm dreaming, and the dream keeps the Forge casting Dunmarrow's children. The sour wells are not illness; they are a god trying to wake up.

Clues.Text: Sexton's ledger of plumbing inspections: 1612, 1631, 1650, onward. Four names each, nineteen years apart, and not one return date entered.
The last four's contract, word for word the party's own, sealed with Alderman Crane's ring and the fee paid in advance by the council.
Casting moulds with Dunmarrow faces in them: the miller's boy, the Crane grandchildren, and faces of people not yet born.
The Verger's letter to the council: 'Send the usual. Something fierce this time; He stirs.' Countersigned, and dated this spring.

Mystery.Payoff: In the Dreaming Hall Maud stops sleepwalking, sits down on the marble, and Gorm speaks through her: slow, kind, apologetic for the size of Himself, and grateful that anyone came. The four clues laid out at her feet make the contract plain, and the party must choose to finish the pilgrimage and wake Him or burn the contract and let the dream, and Dunmarrow's souls, go on.

Tiers.Beat: The Skin: the church Dunmarrow built on a god's chest. Its dead walk the undercrofts in last generation's coats, the Verger's deacon greets you politely, and the alderman's paperwork starts turning up where it should not.

EnterLine.Text: The lychgate stands on His chest. Below it, Dunmarrow laid its dead on Him for six hundred years and called it consecrated ground. First Station: the Skin.

Tiers.Beat: The Gut: the swallow, the crop, the craw. Everything Gorm ate is still alive in here, and so is Grisel Thorn, who has been down nineteen years and did something to earn them.

EnterLine.Text: Below the church the stone turns soft and wet and green, and it is warm, and it moves when nothing should. Second Station: the Gut.

Tiers.Beat: The Heart: the Forge that casts Dunmarrow's souls, tended by men cast without any. Old Ulf shows off the moulds, and the faces in them are known.

EnterLine.Text: Heat, and a beat under the heat. Something here is being made, over and over, and it has never once been asked. Third Station: the Heart.

Tiers.Beat: The Dream: marble halls, the Choir's lullaby, and the truth of the contract. The god turns over; the Verger tightens the gag; the party decides whether to wake Him.

EnterLine.Text: Marble, because He dreams in marble. Somewhere ahead a choir is singing something very old and very soft. Fourth Station: the Dream.

Floors.Title: The Lychgate
Floors.Mood: consecrated ground, a brisk employer, bread in a cellar
Floors.Story: cast_crane sees the party off at the stair with the contract and one sincere line about bread in the first cellar; a Recover quest for his basket plants the counterfoil he would rather nobody read. cast_maud walks past the gate, downward, asleep.

Floors.Title: The Vestibule
Floors.Mood: moss in the mortar, the sexton's lot gone wandering

Floors.Title: The Nave
Floors.Mood: chalk-white bone chapel, a candle nobody needs
Floors.Story: cast_tobit greets the congregation on the Verger's behalf. Decide: tell him the truth, that you are plumbers and not pilgrims (flag told_tobit), or let him keep his saint. Beyond the chancel the wall-press guards the bone-chapel chest.

Floors.Title: The Chantry
Floors.Mood: rotten timber, rising green air, a flustered alderman
Floors.Story: cast_crane has followed the party down to check the invoice and drops the sexton's ledger doing it: clue_ledger, an Investigate across the gas galleries while the chantry fills from the cellars.

Floors.Title: Canon Ludd
Floors.Mood: a liturgy performed by a thing with no congregation

Floors.Title: The Swallow
Floors.Mood: wading in a god's spit, gold teeth in the dark

Floors.Title: The Crop
Floors.Mood: a camp roofed with a spider's shell, a rite nobody asked for

Floors.Title: The Craw
Floors.Mood: tremors, split boulders, strangers who want your teeth

Floors.Title: The Cistern
Floors.Mood: warm sandstone, four levers, a verse carved over each
Floors.Story: cast_crane arrives wheezing to check progress and reads the last four's contract under his own seal: clue_contract, with cast_grisel watching him read it. Decide: forgive her for walking her party to the jailers (flag grisel_forgiven).

Floors.Title: Mother Nit
Floors.Mood: a hatchery ringed in fire; the god has lice

Floors.Title: The Hearth
Floors.Mood: riveted plate, ember light, a cheerful old founder

Floors.Title: The Casting Hall
Floors.Mood: kiln brick, uncast things in cages, keys on a belt
Floors.Story: cast_grisel answers for floor 9: with grisel_forgiven she is an Escort walked out past the jailers to the stairs; without it she wears the jailers' keys herself and the party kills her for them.

Floors.Title: The Mould Room
Floors.Mood: cold steel plate, white lamps, shelves of faces
Floors.Story: cast_ulf shows off his work and hands over clue_moulds: Dunmarrow faces in the casting sand, including Crane's grandchildren, who are not born yet. He is proud of every one.

Floors.Title: The Quench
Floors.Mood: rusted grates under black water, archers on the ledges

Floors.Title: The Bellows
Floors.Mood: red-hot air and a beat that loses count

Floors.Title: The Dream Door
Floors.Mood: veined marble, blue light, singing a long way off
Floors.Story: clue_letter arrives: with told_tobit, cast_tobit brings the Verger's letter to the council himself, defecting; without it cast_maud has it and Tobit's voice is already in the Choir.

Floors.Title: The Windpipe
Floors.Mood: purple gloom, gas climbing the galleries, a confession
Floors.Story: cast_crane admits at the junction that he signed the contract four times and carved the names before the parties left, then betrays the party: Choir stalkers stand where he stood.

Floors.Title: The Dreaming Hall
Floors.Mood: violet dark, one corridor in, a god turning over
Floors.Story: Payoff: cast_maud sits down for the first time and Gorm speaks through her, apologetic for the size of Himself. The four clues are laid out; Decide: finish the pilgrimage and wake Him (flag wake_gorm) or burn the contract and let the dream go on.

Floors.Title: The Last Station
Floors.Mood: cold tiles, three galleries, a verse being finished
Floors.Story: cast_maud channels the rite at the junction: the Waking with wake_gorm, the Unbinding without it, while the Choir breaks on her in waves and the Verger speaks only through the ritual.

Floors.Title: The Mouth
Floors.Mood: pillars for teeth, a floor like a tongue, braziers at the back
Floors.Story: Absalom Quill waits by the throat he has gagged for three hundred years; his half-health and death lines turn on wake_gorm, and so does what the party climbs back into.

Line.Text: Down. Next one, don't dawdle.
That's one less mouth in the throat.
Consecrated ground. It'll soak that up.
Felt worse from a cart horse.
Good. Now I know where you are.
That's coming out of somebody's wages.
Dead men's coin spends the same.
Call it expenses. The contract said expenses.
Still warm. I'll not ask why.
Arm's steadier. Shame about the rest.
Harder going down than I was going in.
Nineteen years of fools taught me that trick.
Big. Big things fall loudest.
Behind me. All of you. Now.
Nobody said god. They said plumbing.
Something's in my head and it's humming.
Hold me down. Hold me down, damn you.
My hands aren't taking orders. Mind the blade.
Not lying down. Not for him.
Floor's warm. That's the worst of it.
Get the others out. Argue later.
Up. Say nothing about it.
I owe you a drink we'll never reach.
Where's my shield. Where is my shield.
That's how it's done. Watch the flank.
Stay down. I mean it.
One. Keep count, somebody.
Clean. Mostly.
Not today. Not by you.
Shield up, blade through. Simple.
He swung first. He'll not swing again.
Rest easy, whatever you were.
Move up. There'll be more.
Are we camping here? Say so and I'll light a fire.
The stairs are that way. Or that way. Pick one. Any one.
I've seen statues with more go in them.
Moss is forming on your boots. I can hear it.
If you're waiting for the dungeon to come to you, it will, and you won't like it.
Move, or I start charging rent for standing in my shadow.
Thinking? Don't strain yourself. Walk and think at the same time; the rest of us manage.
I've held shield walls shorter than this.
Left foot. Then the right. It's a system. Try it.
Fine. I'll go alone, and you can explain to the alderman why.
Dancing is my speciality. Dying, it seems, is yours.
That's how Brand does it. Watch the hips, not the sword.
Down you go, and up go my heels.
Shield, sword, and a little shimmy. Full service.
Who's next? I've got five more of these in me.
Brand's rule: kill it, then shake it.
The shield arm's for blocking. The hips are for this.
Don't tell the captain I can move like this.
Squat, buck, rock. Drill of the day.
That's a soldier's dance. Learned it in a tavern.
Two of each, then back to work. Discipline.
Watch the veteran. Learn something.
I don't do it pretty. I do it done.
My knees disagree with the squats. My knees lost.
There's a wave at the end if you behave.
Stand back. Brand is celebrating.
Even a wall can dance when the enemy's down.
Shields down, hips up.
Call that a funeral march. A quick one.
Right. That's enough feeling good. Where's the next one?
I guess we're getting paid by the mile.
Walking for a living. Didn't see that in the contract.
If I'd wanted to march I'd have stayed in the levy.
My feet have opinions. None of them polite.
Another corridor. Somebody's very proud of these corridors.
Anyone counting the doors? I stopped at forty.
Shield's getting heavy. Nothing to hit with it.
Wake me if something growls.
I've had quieter patrols. Not many.
At this rate the Verger dies of old age before we find him.
Rations are low. Patience is lower.
A fight would be nice. A chair would be nicer.
Left, left, left again. I'm starting to suspect a circle.
The dead are doing a poor job of defending this place.
I've seen livelier graveyards. In fact, this is one.
My sword is sulking. It hasn't been out in an hour.
Somebody hum something. Not Sable.
Mind the puddle. Mind the other puddle.
The alderman said dangerous. The alderman lied, or is bad at walking.
Boots. Stone. Boots. Stone. Gripping stuff.
Quiet as a kept promise.
He had nothing. Typical of this parish.
Don't look. I didn't do it neatly.
That's going to scar somewhere unfashionable.
Rude. I was being so careful.
Bleeding. Fine. I had spare.
Gold teeth. The god won't miss a molar.
Finders, keepers, swallowers, weepers.
Locked. Was locked. Past tense is my trade.
Faster hands. Slower conscience.
I'm improving. The dungeon's improving quicker.
Another trick for a town that won't pay.
Nothing on it worth stealing. Shame.
Brand. You're the wall. Be a wall.
I'll take the flank. The flank is traditional.
Someone else is wearing me. Badly.
Knives out and not by my doing. Run.
It's singing. Gods, it's singing in my teeth.
Pockets first. Then me. I'm joking. Mostly.
I'm not lying down. I'm resting flat.
Don't let the verger write my name neat.
I kept the purse. Priorities.
Up, and I remember every face that waited.
Back from the floor. Charming floor. Hate it.
He had nothing on him. Typical of this parish.
Oh, you'll want to check his pockets. I already did.
From behind. Where the gold is.
Hush now. There. All better.
Nobody saw that. Which is the point.
I liked him better quiet.
Shh. The dead don't haggle.
That one owed me. Now we're square.
You're standing like somebody owes you money. Nobody down here pays.
Shall I pick the lock on your feet?
I've robbed people faster than you decide which way to face.
Go on, dawdle. The rats are taking bets on you.
Don't worry, I'm sure the treasure will wait. Treasure's patient like that. It isn't.
Is this a plan, or did your brain step out for a smoke?
I could rob you blind right now and you'd still be standing here.
Lovely spot. Shall we die in it, or somewhere with better light?
Blink twice if you've forgotten how legs work.
You know the walls don't move, yes? You have to.
Booty be all that, and the booty's all mine.
Look at me go. Look at you not.
Stabbed, dropped, and danced on. The Sable special.
Shake it, Sable. Nobody left to watch but the rats.
Oh, I'm good. I'm so good I'm dancing about it.
Dead. Cue the music.
Stabbed in time with the beat.
That's the knife work done. Now the footwork.
One less partner. Shame, he had rhythm.
Drop. Good. Now watch me not.
Quiet now. I like to dance in silence.
Pockets first, then the hips.
Fell like a drunk on a dance floor. Stays like one too.
Knife in, knife out, step to the left.
I've killed quieter, but never prettier.
Boot on the chest, shimmy to follow.
That one didn't see the blade or the squat coming.
Oh, you dropped something. Everything, actually.
A girl's got to warm up before she dances.
Nothing personal. Everything rhythmic.
Hips don't lie, and neither do I. Much.
Pockets picked, hips kicked. Try and keep up.
Nobody said a girl can't gloat. Watch me gloat.
Two squats, two shimmies, one less problem.
I'd curtsey, but this is better.
A lady celebrates how she likes. This is how I like.
Dead men tell no tales, but this one's getting a dance.
Light fingers, loose hips.
Call it a victory wiggle. I call it Tuesday.
The rats are clapping. Good rats.
If you'd paid up, I'd have danced for you alive.
Shh. Don't talk over the hip rock.
This body was built for stealing and swaying. Mostly swaying.
Another one in the ledger, another little squat.
I take what I like. Tonight I like dancing.
Did somebody just pass gas? Brand. It was Brand.
I could be robbing someone right now. Someone rich. Someone indoors.
A girl walks into a dungeon. That's it. That's the whole joke.
Nothing to steal, nothing to stab. Worst holiday ever.
I spy, with my little eye, something beginning with stone.
If the next room's empty too I'm picking Ilex's pockets for practice.
I've cased houses faster than we're casing this hole.
Who built this? And can I rob them instead?
I'd sing, but Brand said not to. Brand has no ear.
My knives are bored. Bored knives slip.
Twenty more steps and I'm charging a walking fee.
Is it just me, or does every corridor smell of regret?
A lady needs excitement. A lady is getting corridors.
Wake me when there's a lock. Any lock.
I've stolen things that moved more than this dungeon.
Shall we take bets on the next room? I say empty. I always win.
If I see one more torch bracket I'm stealing it out of spite.
Nothing's tried to kill us in ages. I'm almost insulted.
I miss the city. The city had things worth taking.
Walk, walk, walk. My thighs will be magnificent and nobody will see them.
Through the eye. It won't walk back.
One down. I'll want that arrow back.
Nothing down here dies surprised.
Clipped. Still shooting.
Mark the archer on the ledge. I have.
Blood on the string. That slows a draw.
Fletchings. Whoever's they were is past caring.
Someone packed this for a trip home.
Take the rope. Down here rope is kindness.
Steadier draw. The dark's still steadier.
I'm learning His corridors. That frightens me.
Longer sight. Wish I liked what's in it.
Wide target. Thick hide. Keep it at range.
Pillars first, then shoot. Not the reverse.
It's breathing in time with the walls.
Something's drawing my bow for me. Move.
Don't stand in my line. Please don't.
I see through two sets of eyes and one is His.
Quiver's empty anyway. Go on without me.
Count the exits. I counted. Use the second.
The floor's beating. I'd rather it didn't.
Hands on the bow. Good. Step aside.
Thank you. Now watch the high ledges.
Alive, and still owed nineteen years of wages.
Marked it. Loosed. Done.
Two steps closer and it would have been you.
Wind's dead down here. Makes it easy.
It stood still. Its mistake.
Good arrow. Shame about the fletching.
Quiet. Listen for the next one.
Drop. Stay dropped.
I've tracked deer that moved more than you. Dead ones.
Standing still works for a tree. You lack the leaves.
The trail's cold and so are my feet. Walk.
If this is stealth, it's the loud kind.
Two things don't move down here: the dead and you. Keep it to the one.
The arrow doesn't fly until you nock it. Same with you and this corridor.
I count sixty breaths. The dungeon counted them too.
Lost? The way on is the one you're not looking at.
Even a stump knows which way the sun went. Pick a direction.
I'll scout ahead. By which I mean anywhere but here.
One arrow, one corpse, one little dance.
I don't dance for just anyone. You're welcome, dead thing.
The hunt's done. The hips take it from here.
Rangers don't dance, they say. Rangers lie.
Marked, shot, dropped. Now the fun part.
Quiet, both of you. I'm dancing.
Tracked it, dropped it, now I shake it off.
A ranger celebrates once. This is the once.
My arrows fly straight. My hips don't.
Forest rules: kill clean, dance short.
Two squats for the bow, two for the arrow.
I learned this from a stag. Don't ask.
Hunt's over. Hips, you have the floor.
Try the hip rock in a treeline. Builds balance.
I don't smile. I squat.
Something had to die for me to dance. It did.
Nock, loose, wiggle. In that order.
The woods never saw me do this. The woods are lucky.
It stood still. I didn't.
One wave for the dead, then we move.
Fighting for a living is overrated anyway.
No tracks. Nothing's been through here but us and the damp.
I've stalked deer for a day and been less bored.
The wind would tell me something. There's no wind.
My arrows are getting dusty in the quiver.
Mark the wall. We've been here. Twice, now.
Quiet dungeon. Quiet's where things hide. Or where nothing is.
I could track a mouse through this. There are no mice.
Nothing to shoot. I'm counting bricks instead. Four thousand.
Out in the woods there'd be a bird by now. Something.
Anyone else's boots talking to them? Mine won't shut up.
If this is a trail, it's the dullest one I've walked.
A ranger's patience is long. Not this long.
I'll scout ahead. Ahead is more of this.
I miss trees. I'd settle for a shrub.
Nothing moving. I checked. I keep checking.
The bowstring's going slack from boredom. So am I.
Steady pace. Steady nothing.
If something jumps us now I'll thank it.
The stone has no smell. Give me mud and a dead fox any day.
Burned clean. His throat may thank me.
Reduced to component parts. Tidy enough.
That one had a soul cast in a mould. Pity.
My robe. My good robe. My only robe.
Pain is data. I would prefer less data.
Someone intercept the next one, as a courtesy.
Ink, and the hand shook. They knew.
Nineteen years old and still legible. Unlucky.
A reliquary. Nobody tell the priest downstairs.
The words sit easier. The dungeon taught them.
I understand more. I recommend understanding less.
Power, acquired in a stomach. Note the irony.
An organ with opinions. Keep it off me.
I can unmake it. Buy me nine slow breaths.
This was never plumbing. It never once was.
The lullaby is using my mouth. Gag me.
I am two people and the other one is old.
Strike my hands. I'll forgive it. Strike them.
Not lying down. That is his word, not mine.
He dreams. I can hear what He dreams of. Us.
Carry the notes if you can't carry me.
Upright, and considerably less sanguine.
Good. The spell was half said. Stand back.
I saw the memorial stone. My name was neat.
Burned clean. Its throat may thank me.
Fire answers most theological questions.
Observe: it stops when the heat exceeds the will.
I did warn it. Briefly.
Entropy. I merely hurried it along.
Note the smell. Sulphur, mostly. Mostly.
Another argument settled in my favour.
Do try to leave the next one for the sword. My hands are cold.
Fascinating. A man standing in a corridor. I shall write a monograph.
The mind moves the body. In your case the message appears to be lost in transit.
I have watched candles make decisions faster.
Shall I cast Haste on you, or would that only waste the spell?
We are losing light, warmth and, I suspect, brain tissue. Walk.
Contemplation is a virtue. Loitering is merely a habit. Guess which this is.
The door will not open from pure longing. I have tested this.
Is this a tactical pause, or did you forget what feet are for?
Every second you stand there the dungeon grows a little wiser than you. It did not need the help.
Marvellous. We have found the one puzzle you cannot solve: forwards.
Observe: the victory squat. Taught at no academy.
Spell, then shimmy. The second part is not in the grimoire.
I have reduced you to ash, and I shall now wiggle about it.
A scholar's dance. Dignified. Mostly.
Science wins again, and science has rhythm.
Thaumaturgy, then choreography.
The academy would expel me for this hip rock. Worth it.
Two squats: the recommended dose after any incineration.
Observe the mage in motion. Rare. Treasure it.
Cinders settle; a scholar sways.
My robes were not cut for this. I persist.
Fire, then footwork. Both precise.
Ashes to ashes, hips to hips.
The spell cost mana. The dance is free.
A wiggle in the name of natural philosophy.
Let the record show: the mage can move.
Combustion complete. Commence the shimmy.
I calculated the angle of every squat. Flawless.
Dignity is for the unburnt.
Rhythm is merely applied mathematics. Behold.
At this pace my thesis will write itself from boredom.
I have memorised the mortar pattern. It is not interesting.
A spell unused is a spell wasted. I am very wasteful today.
I could enchant a lantern to walk for us. Nobody asked.
The academy never covered tedium. An oversight.
Corridor. Corridor. A rich variety of corridor.
My robes gather dust at a measurable rate. I have measured it.
I count forty-one torches, no foes and one pressing need to sit.
If knowledge is power, I am learning a great deal about flagstones.
Observe: nothing. Again.
Walking is merely falling forwards with manners.
I would summon something to fight, but it would also be bored.
My feet file a formal complaint.
I have begun naming the puddles. This one is Gerald.
A dungeon this empty should be ashamed of itself.
Somebody say something clever. Not Brand.
Fireball. Just to see colour. No? Very well.
My mana regenerates faster than my interest.
The council pays by the floor, not by the fight. Walk on.
Even the echoes have stopped bothering.
Ha! Felt that one in my teeth.
Stand behind me, I said. See why?
Hammer says no.
Another for the stone.
They don't make them like they used to. Good.
Next! My arm's warm now.
Down you go. Mind the step.
Ha! That one had teeth. Gold ones? No. Shame.
Partners, remember. Even shares of whatever that was.
Mind the wet, it'll slip you. Not him. He's done slipping.
I've broken harder rock before breakfast.
Check it for coin. Go on. I'll wait.
Right. Who's next for the lamp?
Not bad for a miner, eh?
Poor iron. It bent.
Don't thank me.
That's what the old man's tools are for.
Patience. They always come to the hammer.
Cast badly. Broke easily.
Next. I've all day.
I've quenched hotter.
Forgive me. Forgive me.
The light held. It held.
I did not want that. I did it.
He would have understood. The Verger. He would.
Stay close. Please. Stay close to the lantern.
Is it... it is. All right. All right.
Saints keep it, whatever it was.

Line.Text: Done, and done badly, but done. Go down. The next page is worse.

ArcNotes: Flags: told_tobit (3) pays on 16; grisel_forgiven (9) pays on 12; wake_gorm (18) pays on 19 and 20. Crane's counterfoil from floor 1 is the first thread of the contract chain: ledger 4, contract 9, moulds 13, letter 16. Crane appears 1, 4, 9, 17 and betrays on 17 only after confessing the memorial stone. Maud is always ahead, always dry, never sits until 18. Ulf never learns what he casts aloud; Tobit's voice joins the Choir if the party let him keep his saint. Bandits (Oddfellows) only in camps.
